chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, and Ali ibn Uthman, from Isحاق ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr). He said: 'The neighbors have more right to it, and there is no objection if you give the value of that in silver.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.فِضَّةً: Silver (used here to denote monetary value)

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to receive Zakat al-Fitr and can it be paid in money?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of *Fitrah* is linked to social solidarity, emphasizing that neighbors hold priority in receiving Zakat al-Fitr to strengthen community bonds. The permissibility of giving the monetary equivalent in silver (*fiḍḍah*) reflects the early Shia scholarly view on the flexibility of the medium of payment, distinguishing it from the later predominant opinion favoring staple foods. This highlights the pragmatic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt in adapting religious obligations to contemporary economic conditions while preserving the spirit of charity.
